chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Our father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Blessed and Exalted God has granted His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) noble characteristics. Test yourselves; if they are in you, praise God, the Mighty and Majestic, and aspire to Him for an increase in them. He mentioned ten of them: Certainty, Contentment, Patience, Gratitude, Satisfaction, Good Character, Generosity, Zeal, Bravery, and Chivalry.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten noble moral characteristics that God granted to the Prophet Muhammad according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a diagnostic method for spiritual self-assessment by linking personal virtue to the Prophet’s exemplary character. The ten listed traits—ranging from internal states like certainty and contentment to external actions like generosity and bravery—serve as a comprehensive framework for ethical development in Shia tradition. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (morality) as a tangible manifestation of faith, inviting believers to actively cultivate these qualities through gratitude and supplication.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-12 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Uthman ibn Isa, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Miskan that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Indeed the Blessed the Sublime God has granted God’s Prophet (MGB) noble characteristics. Try to attain them if you can. If you have them, praise the Honorable the Exalted God and try to reinforce them in yourself. They are as follows: certitude; contentment; perseverance; gratitude; contentedness; being good-tempered; generosity; zeal; bravery and chivalry.”
